service.description: The work orders of the user's maintenance scope (MAINTENANCE_VIEW; with MAINTENANCE_ASSIGNED_VIEW alone, those assigned to the user; PERMISSION_DENIED without), never a template or a step, scoped and filtered in the query before paging: text (id or name), organization, facility (with those inside it), equipment, status (open by default; done; all; or one), kind, source, high priority, overdue, blocked (on hold), mine, an assignee, a team, unassigned, and a window (fromDate, thruDate). Ordered by priority and due. Each row carries its target, organization, assignees, team, window, due, status and the reason it is held; no cost. A holder of MAINTENANCE_ALL_ORGANIZATIONS with an active organization lists that organization's work (F83).

One work order the user may read (a step is read as its root's): its header (target, organization, kind, type, source, severity, priority, the planned window and estimated hours, the actual start and finish, the hold or cancel reason, the outcome and disposition, its team and technicians, its revision), its assignments, its time (a technician with the assigned view sees their own entries and total, never the team's), the user's running timer on it, the lifecycle actions open from its status each allowed or with why not, the completion blockers, and what the user may do (edit, schedule, log time), and its history (the audit log of its status, priority, estimate and target, newest first). No cost.

New ad hoc work (MAINTENANCE_PLAN or _SUPERVISE): a root WorkEffort (WetTask, WepMaintenance, no project, owned by the target's organization, the WorkEffortMaintenance flow) for one target, equipment (assetId; not stock; its facility is the work's) or a facility, in the user's scope, with its MaintenanceWorkOrder row and, for equipment, its primary AssetMaintenance (create#AssetMaintenance, created or scheduled, the planned start as its date, no interval). Corrective work, work a supervisor creates and planned work within the organization's approval threshold in hours are approved on create; other planned work waits in planning for a supervisor (MaintenancePolicy; no estimate is over the threshold). The team defaults to the policy's. A retry with operationKey answers the first root (repeated); changed input under the key is OPERATION_KEY_CONFLICT. Refusals: TARGET_REQUIRED, TARGET_INVALID, NAME_REQUIRED, VALUE_INVALID, DATES_INVALID, TEAM_UNAVAILABLE, RECORD_UNAVAILABLE.

parameter.name: estimatedCompletionDate
parameter.description: The planned finish, the work's due

parameter.name: offlineIntent
parameter.description: Y: starting the work takes its equipment or facility out of service (P5)

parameter.name: templateWorkEffortId
parameter.description: impl-maintenance P6: the procedure the work is made from (approved, in effect, applicable to the target, of the work's organization); its steps become the root's tree in this transaction (ProcessServices.instantiate#WorkProcess' checked path), and the work is never approved on create as corrective work is: the threshold reads the root's estimate with its steps'

parameter.name: roleParties
parameter.description: With a procedure: the person (of the organization) each step role is assigned to; a role named for no one stays a requirement

service.description: An open AssetMaintenance with no linked work (Manufacturing's maintenance request, the baseline's) made into a managed work order (MAINTENANCE_PLAN or _SUPERVISE; its equipment in the user's scope): a root approved, or in progress when the record is, the record its primary AssetMaintenance and linked to the root. Once: a retry, or a second adoption, answers the first root (repeated). Refused: a completed or cancelled record (RECORD_CLOSED; history stays unmanaged), a warranty repair (OWNER_PATH; Customer Service's), one with other linked work (LINKED_WORK).

A work order's header (MAINTENANCE_PLAN or _SUPERVISE; open work only, WORK_CLOSED): name, description, priority, estimated hours (after approval a supervisor's alone, APPROVAL_REQUIRED), type, severity, failure mode, and its target before work starts (equipment work keeps equipment, TARGET_KIND; the same organization, ORGANIZATION_CHANGE; WORK_STARTED), the AssetMaintenance following. At the revision read (RECORD_CHANGED).

The one writer of a work order's assignments (MAINTENANCE_PLAN or _SUPERVISE; open work only): its team (an OrgTeam the organization owns, TEAM_UNAVAILABLE; empty removes it), its technicians (assigneePartyIds replaces the current Assignee rows, ending the others now; each a person employed by or an agent of the organization now, ASSIGNEE_UNAVAILABLE) and its planned window (DATES_INVALID). Scheduling grants no approval. The AssetMaintenance is scheduled with an approved root's window. New technicians are told on MaintenanceWork. At the revision read (RECORD_CHANGED).

parameter.name: replacePartyId
parameter.description: A person replaced on the root and each step of its tree by withPartyId (a leaver's work, Admin's offboarding; impl-maintenance F113)

service.description: The lifecycle of a work order (design §3), the only path to its status: approve (a supervisor; a planner for corrective work or work within the approval threshold, APPROVAL_REQUIRED), start (the assigned technician or a supervisor, NOT_ASSIGNED; actualStartDate, now when empty, never later), hold (a reason, REASON_REQUIRED; no running timer, TIMER_RUNNING; approved work a supervisor's, as the flow's row needs MAINTENANCE_SUPERVISE beside Manufacturing's PRODUCTION_SUPERVISE; work in progress also the assigned technician's), resume (to the status it came from), complete (the assigned technician or a supervisor; no running timer; the outcome, OUTCOME_REQUIRED, and for equipment the disposition, DISPOSITION_REQUIRED; the entered actualCompletionDate, now when empty, written in the same update, never later or before the start), close (a supervisor; completion closes it under the MclOnComplete policy) and cancel (a reason; started work a supervisor's; time, files and history kept). A status the action is not open from is STATUS_INVALID. The primary AssetMaintenance follows. At the revision read (RECORD_CHANGED). Downtime (P5, ResourceOutages.js): start with offline intent (the work order's, or offlineIntent) records the target's outage as planned maintenance (unavailabilityReasonEnumId), or links the one open; complete with equipment still unavailable (MdispUnavailable) records its outage when none is open, and followUpName makes a follow-up corrective work order on the same target, caused by this one and linked to its open outage; completion and cancel restore nothing (end#ResourceUnavailability does). P10: complete with an outside-service line (serviceOrderId, serviceOrderItemSeqId, serviceAcceptedQuantity, the evidence serviceEvidenceContentId and serviceOperationKey) accepts it in the same transaction as accept#MaintenanceService does, under Purchasing's check; completing the work completes no order line.

parameter.name: action
parameter.description: approve, start, hold, resume, complete, close or cancel

service.description: One lifecycle action (transition#MaintenanceWorkOrder) on each of several work orders, each in its own transaction: a result per work order (ok, resultCode, or the refusal's reasonCode and message), the rest going on.
The user's running timer on a work order's tree (assigned; NO_TIMER when none runs there), through TimesheetServices.stop#Timer unchanged.

The user's own time on a work order or step, as start#MaintenanceTimer checks it, by its start and end or its start and hours (HOURS_INVALID, DATES_INVALID; worked, not to come, DATE_FUTURE), through TimeServices.store#TimeEntry unchanged (its timesheet lock applies).

A problem reported on equipment or a facility (MAINTENANCE_REQUEST, PERMISSION_DENIED): a submitted RqtMaintenance request filed by the authenticated party (never a supplied reporter), the target's organization its OrgInternal party, exactly one target (assetId or facilityId of the reporter's own organizations: TARGET_REQUIRED, ONE_TARGET, TARGET_INVALID for stock, RECORD_UNAVAILABLE outside them; organizationPartyId, when given, must be the target's, ORGANIZATION_DENIED) as its RequestRecord, the summary its name (SUMMARY_REQUIRED), the observed time (not later than now, DATE_FUTURE) and the description, a priority 1 to 9, and a photo or other file (contentFile) as RequestContent. A retry under operationKey answers the first request (repeated). An urgent report blocks no equipment.

The equipment and facilities the user may report a problem on (MAINTENANCE_REQUEST; none without): those of the user's own organizations (a Maintenance reader's scope), searched by term in the query ignoring case, each as {value: "asset:id" or "facility:id", label}, with the selected value's label.

The resolver of a report's asset tag scan-input: the equipment a scanned tag (the EquipmentDetail link it holds) or a typed id or serial names, of the organizations the user may report for (MAINTENANCE_REQUEST; nothing without). Its parameters are client input.

Maintenance requests, scoped and filtered in the query before paging: for a planner or supervisor (MAINTENANCE_PLAN or _SUPERVISE) those of their maintenance organizations (organizationPartyId narrows them), for a holder of MAINTENANCE_REQUEST_VIEW_OWN alone the ones they filed (PERMISSION_DENIED without either); by requestId, text (id or name), status (open by default; untriaged; all; or one), target (assetId or facilityId). Each row: the request's name, state (with the reason of a rejected one), priority, date, target and the linked work order's id, name and status; the reporter's name for a planner only. No cost, time, people or other report of the work.

A planner's or supervisor's decision on a maintenance request of their organizations (MAINTENANCE_PLAN or _SUPERVISE; another organization's is RECORD_UNAVAILABLE): create (corrective work, source Reported problem, on the request's target or the one given, which it records; the request's open AssetMaintenance, Manufacturing's, is adopted instead), link (an open work order of the same organization: several reports to one order; WORK_CLOSED, ORGANIZATION_MISMATCH), reject (a reason, REASON_REQUIRED: rejected, duplicate, won't fix, insufficient information, can't reproduce; the request cancelled with it and the comment as a request comment) or assign (the request's assignee, a person of the organization, ASSIGNEE_UNAVAILABLE). Create and link review the request and link it to the work order. A request is triaged once: create again, or link to the same order, answers its work order (repeated); another decision is REQUEST_TRIAGED; a closed request REQUEST_CLOSED. A retry under operationKey answers the first.

The adoption queue (MAINTENANCE_PLAN or _SUPERVISE): open AssetMaintenance records with no work of the user's maintenance organizations (Manufacturing's maintenance requests, the baseline's records), newest first, at most 50, each with the request that asked for it; a warranty repair is Customer Service's and not listed. adopt#MaintenanceRecord, or triage of its request, makes one a work order.

The createMaintenanceRequest action of the mail client's rules (EmailRuleAction ErActCreateMaintenanceRequest, MT-15): a received message to a maintenance team's plus-tag address (MntIntakePlusTag on the team), or to the team the action's value names, becomes a maintenance request of the team's organization, as report#MaintenanceProblem makes one: the sender its reporter (a party found by the address, else a person made from the sender), the team on it, the subject its name, the text its description, the message on it with its attachments as files (file#RequestEmail), and its target the one equipment id the subject names, else none, left for triage. A team is taken only when the rule's owner works for its organization. A message already on a request is left; a reply in a request's thread joins it; with no team the message is an ordinary request (create#RequestFromEmail). Mail text is untrusted: it decides nothing but the target match.

parameter.name: value
parameter.description: The team (partyId), or empty for the plus tag

service.description: A purchase for a work order (MAINTENANCE_PLAN or _SUPERVISE in its organization). Without an order line: a purchase request (RqtPurchase) of the work's organization through Purchasing's create#PurchaseRequest and store#PurchaseRequestItem, the user its requester, linked to the work order by RequestWorkEffort and submitted to Purchasing's approvers unless submit is false; it places and approves nothing (an open work order, WORK_CLOSED; NAME_REQUIRED; Purchasing's refusals of the line). With an order line (orderId, orderItemSeqId): an AssetMaintenanceOrderItem between the work's primary AssetMaintenance and a purchase order line of its organization, never an OrderItemWorkEffort, so maintenance status completes no order line; a line sourced from one of the work's requests is the work's, another is linked only by a buyer (PURCHASE_ORDER_EDIT, else PERMISSION_DENIED); facility work has no AssetMaintenance (LINK_UNAVAILABLE). A retry with operationKey answers the first request (repeated).

Internal to the RequestItemOrder entity ECA MaintenancePurchaseSourced: when Purchasing sources a line of a purchase request linked to managed equipment work, the work's primary AssetMaintenance is linked to the order line (AssetMaintenanceOrderItem). Only a RequestItemOrder that exists is followed; nothing else changes.

A work order's purchases for its reader: its purchase requests with their lines and state, and the purchase order lines that fulfil it (linked, or sourced from its requests), each with its supplier, order state, quantity and, for a service line, what was accepted and is left; prices only for a buyer, a price reader or a maintenance cost reader. Whether the user may request (a planner or supervisor, the work open), link a line (a buyer, equipment work) and accept outside service (the assigned technician or a supervisor with Purchasing's PURCHASE_ORDER_EDIT or STOCK_RECEIVE, the work in progress, held or complete), with the work's files as evidence.

Accept outside service of a work order (CompleteWork's "Accept outside service", also open from the Purchasing tab): a service line of the work (LINE_UNLINKED otherwise), by its assigned technician or a supervisor (NOT_ASSIGNED), the work in progress, held or complete (STATUS_INVALID), through Purchasing's mantle.order.OrderServices.accept#ServiceItem under its own check (PURCHASE_ORDER_EDIT or STOCK_RECEIVE, PERMISSION_DENIED; the buying organization; at most as ordered; once under operationKey) with the work order and its evidence: a file of the work (workEffortContentId; EVIDENCE_INVALID) attached to the order line as OrderContent once. The line is linked to the work's primary AssetMaintenance.

A purchase order as Maintenance reads it (OrderDetail at Maintenance/WorkOrders/OrderDetail; crosscut §3.6): read only, for a maintenance work reader, its lines that fulfil work orders the user reads (linked to a work's AssetMaintenance or sourced from its purchase request), each with its work orders, quantity, required date and what was accepted; prices only for a price reader. An order linked to none of the user's work is RECORD_UNAVAILABLE.

Purchasing's RequestDetail's originating work (design-purchasing "Maintenance purchases"): for a user who reads the purchase request under Purchasing's rule (its people, or PURCHASE_ORDER_EDIT, PURCHASE_APPROVE, SUPPLY_PLAN_VIEW or SUPPLY_PLAN_RUN in its organization), the work orders it was raised from: id, name, target, status and need date, and whether Maintenance opens it for them (canOpen); never its notes, time or people.
